title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 58
description: Ten questions on Psalms 58: unjust judges, wicked people like a deaf cobra, and the prayer that God will break their teeth and judge the earth.

questions.text: What does the psalmist call the ones he asks whether they speak righteousness?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:1 asks, "Do you indeed speak righteousness, silent ones?"

questions.text: What do they plot in their heart?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:2 says, "In your heart you plot injustice."

questions.text: From when do the wicked go astray?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:3 says the wicked go astray from the womb and are wayward as soon as they are born.

answers.text: From the day they became rich
From the day they became kings

questions.text: Their poison is compared to the poison of what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:4 says their poison is like the poison of a snake, like a deaf cobra that stops its ear.

questions.text: To whose voice does the deaf cobra not listen?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:5 says it doesn't listen to the voice of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be.

questions.text: Whose great teeth does the psalmist ask Yahweh to break out?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:6 says, "Break out the great teeth of the young lions, Yahweh."

questions.text: Like what does the psalmist ask that they vanish?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:7 says, "Let them vanish like water that flows away."

questions.text: Which creature that melts and passes away is mentioned in verse 8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:8 says, "Let them be like a snail which melts and passes away."

questions.text: What will the righteous do when he sees the vengeance?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:10 says the righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance.

questions.text: What will men say at the end of the psalm?
questions.explanation: Psalms 58:11 says men shall say there is a reward for the righteous and a God who judges the earth.

answers.text: There is a God who judges the earth
God rests far away from men
The wicked will never be judged
